 Judgment
1. This Appeal is by the claimants for enhancement of compensation.

4.83 Ares of land belonging to the claimants was acquired as per Section 4(1) Notification dated 25/09/2001 under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for the purpose of establishing Polytechnic under the Institute of Human Resources Development (IHRD).
The subject land is included in category No. 3 having panchayat road access.
The Land Acquisition Officer fixed land value at the rate of Rs. 24,879/- per Are.
On reference, the Court fixed the land value at Rs.39,806/- per Are.
2. I heard the learned counsel for the appellant Sri.Siju Kamalasanan, the learned Senior Government Pleader for the 1st respondent, Smt. Rekha C. Nair.

3. The learned counsel for the appellant argued that in Ext.A2 judgment, another judgment in L.A.R.
No. 366/1997 was relied .

2025:KER:39162 LA.APP. NO. 110 OF 2014 on, in which the land value was fixed at Rs. 75,000/-
per Are.
The said land was acquired for the Model Polytechnic, Karunagappally.
It is adjacent to the acquired land.
Section 4(1) Notification in the said case is dated 10.12.1999.

Considering the nearness of the property covered in L.A.R. No. 366/1997 with the acquired property and the time difference between the Section 4(1) Notification, the Reference Court should have given more than Syamala Devi vs The Kerala State on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13748894/
2 Rs.75,000/- per Are to the claimants.
4.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned Senior Government Pleader opposed the said prayer by contending that, even though Exts.A1 and A2 judgment in another two Land Acquisition references were produced before the Reference Court, the claimants did not take out any commission to compare the said properties with the acquired land.
Even the claimants in those judgments were also not examined.
Hence the said judgments or the judgment relied thereon are not to be considered.
I have considered the rival contentions.
6. It is seen that no commission was taken by the claimants to compare Exts.A1 and A2 properties with the acquired property.
The learned counsel for the appellant is attempting to persuade this Court to rely on the judgment in L.A.R No. 366/1997.
According to the learned counsel, the said property and the acquired property are situated in the same compound.
The said Judgment is not produced before the Reference Court.
I am unable to accept the said contention for the reason since the claimant has not produced the said judgment.
In the absence of any data for comparison, this Court cannot rely on Exts.A1 and A2 judgment and the judgment in L.A.R. No. 366/1997.

But considering the fact that Exts.A1 and A2 properties belong to the same village and the property of the claimant is situated on the side of the panchayat road, I deem it fit to fix the land value at the rate of Rs. 45,000/- per Are for the acquired land.

Accordingly, this Land Acquisition Appeal is allowed with proportional cost re-fixing the land value for the acquired land value of 4.83 Ares from the claimants at Rs. 45,000/- per Are, which includes the land value awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer.

The claimants are entitled to get all the statutory benefits including interest.
